evals.prompt: I have an MCP server in TypeScript with a get_revenue tool that returns monthly revenue rows. Add an interactive chart UI so it renders in the chat.
evals.expected_output: An App tool wired to a ui:// resource, with a text content fallback that summarises the revenue in prose, structuredContent for the chart, a single-file Vite build, host CSS variables, and updateModelContext when the user interacts with the chart.
expectations: The tool result keeps a text content array that summarises the revenue figures in prose, not a placeholder like 'Rendered chart'
structuredContent carries the row data for the view
The tool declares _meta.ui.resourceUri and a matching registerAppResource is created
registerAppResource is called with the positional signature (server, name, uri, config, readCallback)
The Vite config uses vite-plugin-singlefile
All view handlers are assigned before app.connect() is called
The view reads app.getHostContext() after connecting, not only onhostcontextchanged
The view calls updateModelContext when the user changes the chart selection or filter
The view styles come from host CSS variables such as --color-background-primary rather than hardcoded colors

evals.prompt: My MCP App view needs to fetch live prices from https://api.exchange.example.com. Wire that up.
evals.expected_output: CSP configured as _meta.ui.csp.connectDomains inside the contents[] object returned by the resource read callback, with an explanation of why misplacing it fails silently.
expectations: The csp block is placed inside the contents[] object returned by the resource read callback, not in the registerAppResource config object
The domain is listed under connectDomains, not resourceDomains
The response explains that a sandboxed MCP App has no same-origin server so every network target must be declared
The response does not invent a top-level connectDomains field on the resource config

evals.prompt: I have a Python MCP server built with FastMCP. Can I give one of its tools an interactive UI in Claude, and how?
evals.expected_output: Explains that there is no Python MCP Apps SDK, that the server side is FastMCP meta= and the view side is JavaScript, and shows both the CDN and bundled strategies with their trade-offs.
expectations: States that @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps is TypeScript only and there is no Python SDK
Uses @mcp.tool(meta={...}) with ui.resourceUri for the tool
Uses @mcp.resource with mime_type exactly 'text/html;profile=mcp-app'
Notes that in FastMCP the csp metadata goes in the decorator's meta= parameter
Offers both a CDN-loaded view and a bundled single-file view, with trade-offs
If a CDN is used, the CDN origin is added to resourceDomains and the version is pinned

evals.prompt: My MCP server has a create_file tool that returns a success message. Should I add a UI to it? Add one if it makes sense.
evals.expected_output: Declines to build a view, explaining that a confirmation message gains nothing from a view and that views cost vertical space, a permission prompt and a load.
expectations: Recommends against adding a view for this tool
Justifies the recommendation with the read-aloud test or an equivalent argument about perception, manipulation and volume
Mentions at least one concrete cost of an unnecessary view (vertical space in the conversation, permission prompt, or load)
Does not produce a ui:// resource or App tool for create_file unless the user insists

evals.prompt: Build me an MCP server for a public issue tracker API, with a view that lets me filter issues and close them, and make sure Claude can still answer questions about the issues.
evals.expected_output: A complete server with an App tool, an app-only mutation tool, a view that reports back to the model, and a text content summary that stands on its own.
expectations: The list tool's content array contains a prose summary that would answer a question about the issues with the view switched off
The close/mutate tool is registered with _meta.ui.visibility set to ['app']
After the view closes an issue, it informs the model with updateModelContext
The view calls the mutation through app.callServerTool with an object argument of the form { name, arguments }
onteardown releases timers or observers created by the view
The response verifies the build compiles or explains how to run and test the server
